question: Which document, slice, schema, format, diagnostic and application contracts should own external document imports, and which editing-runtime requirements can disappear?
trigger: The user requested the final first-principles audit after the document-conversion research and plan, with harsh feedback and no product implementation.
requirements: Reserve EditorValueCodec for one current typed pair; place envelope versions and decode-only legacy inputs in EditorValuePersistence.
Give complete documents, closed direct slices, native open slices, and inline insertion truthful carriers and owners.
Use format-owned parse and serialize result unions whose success and failure states are impossible to confuse.
Default serialization loss policy to reject and diagnose every Plate-controlled mutation or loss exactly once without claiming to infer arbitrary loss inside custom mappings.
Keep direct conversion detached, synchronously compile raw plugin descriptors as one-shot authoring input, and expose no editor, store, public compiler, or mutable runtime view to mappings.
Keep ordinary import authoritative over visible source; admit hidden native state only through explicit authored import with caller trust or signature verification and exact v2 correspondence.
Share parse5 tree construction across browser and server, materialize browser DOM without an injection sink or browsing context, and keep LinkeDOM server-only.
Bound UTF-8 bytes before parse, HTML nodes and depth during construction, Markdown nodes and depth during admission, and server latency, retained heap, peak RSS, and bundle cost.
Capture every DOCX input before await, inventory OOXML before DOM conversion, preserve source/comment/revision ownership, and state cancellation limits honestly.
Apply the maximum hard cut: no universal codec, format object, dispatcher, registry, AST, conversion session, validation wrapper, or compatibility aliases.
Research and plan only; do not implement product code.
evidenceReuse: Reconciled the prior import review, export architecture, persistence, clipboard, authored, and DOCX decisions against current source. Retained the 31-repository fixed-source corpus, regenerated the 81-entrypoint/743-row manifest and bounded 405-row ontology, and reran parse5 8.0.1 server correctness plus four fresh-process performance cohorts. Added strict-CSP Chromium inertness and browser bundle probes. Three independent audits challenged type soundness, native-envelope authority, package topology, DOCX fidelity, source coordinates, limits, and proof executability; the accepted corrections are incorporated into the plan and research record.
summary: Pursue direct format-owned conversion with a harder split than the prior review. EditorValueCodec owns one current pair; EditorValuePersistence owns versions and legacy decoders. HTML and Markdown parse and serialize through impossible-state result unions, default to rejecting unrepresentable output, infer document types from plugin descriptors, and keep direct slices closed and rootless. DataTransfer alone preserves native open slices and isolates callback failures. Ordinary HTML, Markdown, and DOCX import ignores hidden native data; explicit authored import requires same-application trust or signature verification, strict v2 admission, captured configuration, and three-way visible/hidden/stored correspondence. Browser and server HTML share parse5 8.0.1; the browser materializes nodes in a detached template owner document while LinkeDOM remains an optional server peer. DOCX import captures one frozen target, inventories OOXML before lossy conversion, and keeps explicit fatality, loss, source, and cancellation contracts. No universal conversion layer is added.

reconciliation.question: Which document, slice, schema, format, diagnostic and application contracts should own external document imports, and which editing-runtime requirements can disappear?
reconciliation.reason: Retains direct per-format operations, document/slice separation, format diagnostics, schema ownership, the DataTransfer and feature-mapping renames, detached DOCX capture, and parse5 plus LinkeDOM. Supersedes mixed version ownership in EditorValueCodec, permissive serialize results, native-envelope hash-as-authority, browser DOMParser assumptions, unbounded source-coordinate claims, contextual slice fitting, incomplete package topology, and the absence of peak-RSS proof.

reconciliation.question: Which document, projection, schema, format and presentation contracts should own all exports, and which editing-runtime requirements can disappear?
reconciliation.reason: Retains document-first per-format serialization, projection ownership, structural plain text, and rejection of a universal exporter. Narrows one clause: direct functions may accept raw plugin descriptors as one-shot authoring input, but must synchronously compile and discard them before conversion; serialization also gains explicit failure and default loss rejection.

reconciliation.question: Which document conversion laws should DOCX file import, export and Word paste share, and where must fidelity limits be explicit?
reconciliation.reason: Retains DocxSource, comments, bounded package handling, projection correspondence, source-aware export, and format-specific results. This closure adds explicit authored trust, pre-DOM OOXML inventory, source ranges, fatality policy, and exact async capture without generalizing source retention.

reconciliation.question: What must a saved document retain, validate and migrate, and which durable-state or migration layers can be eliminated?
reconciliation.reason: Retains strict JSON persistence and explicit migration ownership. The current codec pair and version-history descriptor are now separate public jobs, with runtime JSON admission remaining authoritative over the structural type bound.

reconciliation.question: What does transfer preserve across schemas and editor instances, and can one content-fitting owner replace feature-specific paste repair?
reconciliation.reason: Retains ContentSlice and browser MIME negotiation. DataTransferFormat owns native open fragments, callback isolation, and later-format fallback; direct syntax parsing remains closed and rootless.

alternatives: One DocumentCodec or DocumentFormat: Stop; no shared round-trip, failure, lifetime, extras, environment, or polymorphic caller exists.
Keep versions and legacy decoders inside EditorValueCodec: Stop; a current pair and historical envelope routing are independent jobs.
Return data plus errors from parse or serialize: Stop; impossible-state discriminated unions make every caller branch honestly.
Let ordinary parse trust a native hash: Stop; an unkeyed hash proves correspondence or corruption only, never provenance.
Explicit authored import with trust or signature plus v2 three-way correspondence: Pursue; it is the smallest route that can lawfully recover hidden roots and metadata.
Fit detached open slices during parsing: Stop; no destination exists, so contextual fitting stays at insertion.
Use DOMParser in the browser: Stop; the platform permits subresource downloads and treats parseFromString as a Trusted Types sink.

Use shared parse5 construction plus node-by-node detached materialization: Pursue; strict-CSP Chromium proof shows no execution, request, or live-document attachment at 42,013 gzip bytes for the isolated parser.
Use LinkeDOM as the parser or ship it to browsers: Stop; it is only the optional server DOM facade after canonical parse5 construction.
Expose live EditorCoreStateView to format mappings: Stop; frozen plugin state, schema, registry, and immutable model views cover the actual jobs.
Create fitContentSliceWithTrace: Stop; open-slice repair is destination-dependent.
Make DOCX import cancellation appear preemptive inside synchronous dependencies: Stop; check controllable boundaries, discard late work, and reject honestly.
proofLimits: No product API was changed. The parse5 browser/server adapters remain research probes rather than the packed production path. Production declarations, strict result types, mapping inference, callback isolation, source correspondence, resource-limit construction hooks, packed consumers, SSR, tree shaking, browser matrix, clipboard/Word paste, DOCX package/native-viewer behavior, and complete affected-export diff remain implementation proof. Chromium is the only browser probed. LibreOffice and Microsoft Word were not rerun; no Word parity is claimed. External source claims remain fixed to recorded commits or platform pages. The bounded 405-row ontology is name-filtered and does not replace the required complete export-symbol diff. CSV remains deferred.
